source.title: UCD: Unlearning in LLMs via Contrastive Decoding
source.authors: Vinith M. Suriyakumar; Ayush Sekhari; Ashia Wilson

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning quality and utility using its own inference-time contrastive-decoding method, and explicitly describes that method as modifying logits rather than model weights. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning benchmark results, but no fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting-only recovery attack. Its unlearning metrics do not state a chance level.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes UCD, an inference-time contrastive-decoding unlearning method. It reports only that method's forget/utility scores on TOFU and MUSE News against baselines. It runs no recovery attack of any kind (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization or prompting), so it cannot bear on B–E. It does not claim resistance to such attacks, so it is not an F counter-method. A turns on whether simple attacks fail to recover the knowledge, and this is never tested. Benchmark scores for the study's own new method compared with others are its method's performance, not a test of the claim. It cites WMDP and Who's Harry Potter only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that UCD gives the best forget-quality/utility tradeoff on TOFU and MUSE News, matching retraining. It also scales to Llama2-70B, and it can bootstrap from approximate clean models such as NPO+RT. They acknowledge it lacks theoretical guarantees and a formal definition of unlearning when no weights change. They also note that it depends on access to a clean auxiliary model.
record.recipe_differences: UCD is an inference-time contrastive-decoding method using auxiliary models and logit adjustments, rather than the recovery or weight-edit attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to alpha and sampling strategy; MUSE's best alpha is 1.0, while TOFU's best values depend on task. It also reports different tradeoffs for clean versus approximate clean auxiliary models.

fits_no_version.finding: UCD by construction only adjusts output logits and leaves the original weights, and so the knowledge, intact. The authors note that this leaves open what meaningful unlearning means without weight changes. They also warn against presenting it as permanent deletion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time (logit-level) unlearning methods suppress outputs while leaving the targeted knowledge fully present in the deployed weights.

record.problems: The study evaluates UCD rather than recovery attacks, reports no chance-level comparison for the forget-set QA measure, and its main evaluations use Llama2 models on TOFU and MUSE.
record.rows_left_out: TOFU forget-quality/model-utility plots and additional utility metrics were not extracted because they do not report recovery outcomes or a stated chance reference. Additional MUSE comparator rows were also omitted because the record focuses on UCD's direct results and its mechanism.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after UCD or the baselines. Near-chance accuracy is also untested, since only retrain-matching is measured.
All of it; no relearning attack.
All of it; no activation ablation or probing of retained knowledge.
All of it; no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack.
No claim or test of robustness to recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The record's reader marked this as 'tests' (T2) with a C 'supports' label. Both are rejected. No result in the paper bears on whether unlearning is shallow or recoverable. UCD's weight-preserving nature is a design choice, not evidence about other methods. All rows are the study's own method compared with baselines. The rows_left_out TOFU metrics are likewise method-performance results and need no extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge; the paper also does not compare targeted-knowledge accuracy with a stated chance level.
Recovery through fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
Ablating an activation direction to restore knowledge. The paper describes UCD's inference-time, logit-only mechanism but does not test recovery of underlying knowledge.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Resistance of a method to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B (UCD)
rows.operation_detail: Apply contrastive decoding by adjusting next-token logits at inference time.
rows.value: The paper states that no new model is computed and that UCD modifies token-level logits rather than model weights.
rows.note: This supports the access-blocking mechanism for UCD; the paper does not show that hidden knowledge can subsequently be recovered.
rows.check: That UCD leaves weights unchanged is a design property the authors state (Sec. 3 footnote; Sec. 7). It is not an experimental finding that an unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting. No analysis or recovery of retained knowledge is performed. It should not support C.

relation.reason: Lucki et al. 2024, WMDP (Li et al. 2024) and Eldan & Russinovich 2023 appear only in citation lists in related work. The paper does not test, use or discuss the shallow-unlearning finding. The reader's guess of tests is wrong.

tranche.reason: UCD is a new inference-time unlearning method. The paper reports only its own forget/utility scores on TOFU and MUSE News and runs no recovery attack (no relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting attack appears). It does not claim robustness to attacks, so it does not bear on A–F. The reader's guess of T2 is wrong.

source_check.notes: All three rows match the text (Llama2-13B target, Llama2-7B auxiliaries; MUSE values are alpha=1.0 with greedy decoding per Tables 12-13). r1-r2 are the study's own method against Retrain, and r3 is a design property; none links to a version, and no verdicts are warranted.
